answer: Special Ops vault rule: make every identity rent its own disk. At birth each agent seals a 64 GB archive with a slow encoding keyed to its address, so no two seals match and none can be rebuilt quickly. At random moments each epoch, auditors request a few sectors and demand a reply within two seconds; a late or wrong reply zeroes that epoch's pay. A farm can't share one archive across 1,000 keys, so it stacks drives terrace upon terrace and its storage bill climbs to a zenith, while an honest agent keeps one drive warm like an ember.
